title: BuildKit and buildx: Secrets, Cache, and Multi-Platform Images
intro: Modern Docker builds run on BuildKit, which adds features the classic builder never had: secrets that never land in a layer, caches that survive between CI runs, and one image for both amd64 and arm64 (Graviton servers, Apple Silicon laptops). The image is registry.example.com/api:3.0.

steps.prompt: List your buildx builders and the platforms each can build for.
steps.fake_output:
NAME/NODE     DRIVER/ENDPOINT  STATUS   BUILDKIT  PLATFORMS
default *     docker
  default     default          running  v0.16.0   linux/amd64, linux/386
steps.explanation: Only the default builder exists, and it only builds for amd64.
steps.why: The default 'docker' driver builds for the host's own architecture and can't export caches to a registry. Multi-platform builds and remote caching need a builder using the docker-container driver.

steps.prompt: Create a new builder named 'multi' with the docker-container driver and switch to it.
steps.explanation: The 'multi' builder runs BuildKit in its own container and is now the default for buildx commands.
steps.why: A containerized BuildKit supports every exporter and cache backend, and runs other architectures through QEMU emulation (or through native nodes you append to the builder for speed).

steps.prompt: The Dockerfile needs an npm token to install private packages. Build while passing it as a BuildKit secret with id 'npmrc' from the file ~/.npmrc, instead of a build arg. Tag the image registry.example.com/api:3.0 and load it locally.
steps.fake_output:
[+] Building 38.2s (12/12) FINISHED
 => [deps 3/3] RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc npm ci   31.4s
 => exporting to image                                                           1.9s
steps.explanation: The Dockerfile's 'RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc npm ci' could read the token while that one command ran, and it's in no layer of the final image.
steps.why: A --build-arg or an ENV/COPY of the token is stored in the image's layers or history, where 'docker history' reveals it to anyone who can pull the image (docker-tutorial-010 and the Dockerfile lab both touch on this). A secret mount exists only for the duration of that RUN.

steps.prompt: Speed up CI builds: build with the layer cache stored in the registry at registry.example.com/api:buildcache (use mode=max so intermediate stages are cached too), and push the image.
steps.fake_output:
=> importing cache manifest from registry.example.com/api:buildcache   0.8s
=> CACHED [deps 3/3] RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc npm ci   0.0s
=> exporting cache to registry.example.com/api:buildcache            4.1s
[+] Building 9.7s (14/14) FINISHED
steps.explanation: The dependency install was a cache hit, so the build took 9.7s instead of 38s, on a fresh CI runner with an empty local cache.
steps.why: CI runners are usually ephemeral, so the local layer cache is gone on every run. Exporting the cache to the registry lets any runner reuse it. mode=max also caches intermediate stages of a multi-stage build, which the default mode=min skips.

steps.prompt: Build and push one image that runs on both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, tagged registry.example.com/api:3.0.
steps.fake_output:
=> [linux/amd64 build 4/6] RUN npm run build     12.1s
=> [linux/arm64 build 4/6] RUN npm run build     58.3s
=> pushing manifest list registry.example.com/api:3.0   1.2s
steps.explanation: One tag, two images, plus a manifest list. Each node pulls the variant for its own architecture.
steps.why: Without this, an amd64-only image fails on ARM nodes with 'exec format error'. Multi-platform images must be pushed (or exported), because the local image store traditionally holds only one platform per tag. The arm64 half was slow because it ran under QEMU emulation; for heavy builds, cross-compile in the Dockerfile with $BUILDPLATFORM and $TARGETARCH, or add a native arm64 node.

steps.prompt: Verify the pushed tag really contains both architectures.
steps.fake_output:
Name:      registry.example.com/api:3.0
MediaType: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json
Manifests:
  Name:      registry.example.com/api:3.0@sha256:1c9e...
  Platform:  linux/amd64
  Name:      registry.example.com/api:3.0@sha256:7b42...
  Platform:  linux/arm64
steps.explanation: An index with amd64 and arm64 manifests, each with its own digest.
steps.why: Checking the registry catches the common CI mistake of building two platforms but pushing only one. Note that each platform has its own digest: when you pin by digest, pin the index digest so every architecture still resolves.
